### A Peninnah Problem - One Year Devotions for Women
Author: Jill Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-women/a-peninnah-problem-one-year-devotions-for-women-february-5.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 1:6-7
Points:
- Many people face a "Peninnah" in life who inflicts persistent cruelty and emotional pain.
- Hannah responded to recurring taunts not with retaliation, but by pouring out her sorrow to the Lord in prayer.
- Entrusting heavy emotional burdens to God restores our peace and joy even before circumstances change.
- True spiritual victory comes when our hearts learn to rejoice primarily in God rather than in earthly gifts.

### Day 4: 1 Samuel 1:1–8
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-4-1-samuel-1-18.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 1:1-8
Points:
- Elkanah's polygamous household violated God's creation design for marriage, creating chronic relational distress.
- Common cultural practices do not equate to divine approval, because God's standards do not shift with public opinion.
- Elkanah was insensitive and self-absorbed when trying to comfort Hannah, failing to truly understand her grief.
- Husbands must actively engage in family life and make real efforts to empathize with their wives.
